security_audit.summary: Most static detections are false positives from Markdown fences, reference URLs, CSS, and example text. The executable pipeline template does perform local file writes and cleanup using unvalidated batch and item identifiers. No evidence found of credential exfiltration, malicious network access, shell execution, or embedded prompt injection commands.

remediation.issue: Unvalidated batch and item identifiers can affect filesystem paths.
remediation.suggestion: Restrict identifiers to safe slugs, resolve paths, and enforce that all writes and deletes stay under data and output roots.

remediation.issue: Cleanup deletes files under paths derived from user supplied identifiers.
remediation.suggestion: Add path confinement checks before unlink operations and require confirmation for cleanup outside a temporary workspace.

remediation.issue: Source content is inserted directly into the example LLM prompt.
remediation.suggestion: Delimit untrusted content clearly and test adversarial inputs that try to override formatting or analysis instructions.

semantic_findings.title: Unvalidated Path Components in Pipeline Template
semantic_findings.description: The executable template builds data and output paths from batch_id and item_id without validating safe path segments. A crafted identifier could redirect writes or cleanup outside the intended directories.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: batch_id comes from CLI input and is joined with data and output roots. Exploitability depends on user input and source customization, so confidence is high but not absolute.

semantic_findings.title: Prompt Injection Exposure in Example LLM Pipeline
semantic_findings.description: The template places source title and content directly into an LLM prompt without explicit untrusted-data handling. Malicious source content could alter the requested format or manipulate downstream parsing.
semantic_findings.confidence_reasoning: The prompt interpolation is direct and source content is treated as model input. No malicious payload is present in the skill, so this is an exposure rather than an active attack.

content.value_statement: LLM projects fail when teams automate before validating task fit, cost, and architecture. This skill guides Claude, Codex, and Claude Code through validation, pipeline design, estimation, and iteration.
actual_capabilities: Evaluates whether a task fits LLM strengths before automation.
Designs acquire, prepare, process, parse, and render pipeline stages.
Uses file based state patterns for caching, retries, and debugging.
Plans structured output prompts and resilient parsing rules.
Estimates batch processing costs from item counts and token assumptions.
Provides a Python pipeline template with CLI stages.
limitations: Does not make external API calls unless users customize the template.
Does not guarantee model output quality or parsing reliability.
Requires users to verify current model prices and availability separately.
Template paths need review before use with untrusted identifiers.

use_cases.title: Validate a New LLM Idea
use_cases.description: Check task fit, expected error tolerance, output needs, and manual prototype steps before building automation.

use_cases.title: Design a Batch Pipeline
use_cases.description: Map data acquisition, prompt preparation, LLM processing, parsing, and final rendering into separate stages.

use_cases.title: Choose an Agent Architecture
use_cases.description: Compare simple pipelines, single agents, and multi-agent designs against context, cost, and complexity limits.

prompt_templates.title: Validate Task Fit
prompt_templates.scenario: Beginner planning for a possible LLM feature.
prompt_templates.prompt: Evaluate whether this task fits an LLM workflow. Identify inputs, desired outputs, error tolerance, manual prototype steps, and reasons to use traditional code instead. Task: [describe task].

prompt_templates.title: Design a Batch Pipeline
prompt_templates.prompt: Design a staged batch pipeline for this workload. Include acquire, prepare, process, parse, and render stages. Explain file state, retries, caching, and test checkpoints. Workload: [describe workload].

prompt_templates.title: Estimate Cost and Scale
prompt_templates.prompt: Estimate the cost and scale risks for this LLM pipeline. Use item count, input tokens, output tokens, retries, parallelism, and model choice. State assumptions clearly. Pipeline: [describe pipeline].

prompt_templates.title: Review Architecture Tradeoffs
prompt_templates.scenario: Advanced review of an existing design.
prompt_templates.prompt: Review this LLM project architecture for unnecessary complexity, weak task-model fit, parsing risks, prompt injection exposure, cost surprises, and simpler alternatives. Architecture: [paste design].

output_examples.input: A team wants to summarize 2,000 support tickets with an LLM.
output_examples.output: The skill recommends a manual sample first, then a staged batch pipeline. It flags token cost, classification accuracy, retry handling, and structured parsing as planning items.

output_examples.input: A developer asks whether to build a multi-agent research system.
output_examples.output: The skill compares a simple pipeline with a multi-agent design. It recommends multi-agent only when context isolation or parallel research justifies added cost.

output_examples.input: A data analyst needs a repeatable LLM report generator.
output_examples.output: The skill outlines separate acquire, prepare, process, parse, and render stages. It adds caching, cost estimation, and parser failure handling.

best_practices: Validate one representative example manually before writing automation.
Keep LLM calls in a separate, cacheable process stage.
Estimate cost early and track actual usage during development.
anti_patterns: Building a full pipeline before testing task-model fit.
Combining acquisition, LLM calls, parsing, and rendering in one script.
Assuming structured model output will always match the requested format.

faq.question: What type of projects does this skill support?
faq.answer: It supports LLM batch pipelines, agent-assisted development plans, architecture choices, and cost estimation workflows.

faq.question: Does it call external services by default?
faq.answer: No. The included Python template uses a mock LLM response until users add their own API client.

faq.question: Can it help decide if an LLM is unnecessary?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes criteria for choosing traditional code when precision, latency, or determinism matter more.

faq.question: Does it include runnable code?
faq.answer: Yes. It includes a Python batch pipeline template that creates local data and output files.

faq.question: What should users review before running the template?
faq.answer: Users should review file paths, batch identifiers, item identifiers, and cleanup behavior in a safe working directory.

faq.question: Can it design multi-agent systems?
faq.answer: It can compare single pipeline and multi-agent approaches, but deeper multi-agent implementation needs separate design work.
